question: What do blood disorders primarily affect?

options.A: Chronic electrical malfunctions of the heart muscle
options.B: Primary infections of the digestive tract lining
options.C: Conditions affecting blood components and plasma
options.D: Abnormalities restricted only to bone structure

explanation: Blood disorders are all about our blood cells, platelets, and plasma. You've got this! Think of them as troubles within our body's transport system. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h1)

question: Why is the nursing process so helpful when caring for patients with blood disorders?

options.A: It stops patients from ever developing secondary hospital infections
options.B: It completely replaces the need for routine physician medical orders
options.C: It offers a systematic framework to manage complex and systemic pathologies
options.D: It guarantees that laboratory values will return to normal overnight

explanation: Because blood flows everywhere, a blood disorder affects the whole body. Using the nursing process helps you stay organized and keep your patient safe step-by-step! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h1)

question: Which area is best for checking pallor (paleness) in a patient with dark skin?

options.A: The outer surface of the earlobes
options.B: The dorsal surface of both feet
options.C: The palms of the hands and fingertips
options.D: Conjunctiva of the eyes and oral mucosa

explanation: Great clinical skill here! Checking inside the mouth or eyelids gives a truer picture of color changes when pigmented skin makes pallor hard to spot. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h2)

question: What sign would you most expect in a patient with a low platelet count?

options.A: Stiff neck and high fever spikes

explanation: Platelets help us stop bleeding. When they're low, tiny red spots (petechiae) or bleeding gums show us that clotting isn't happening properly. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h2)

question: Why do we use the nursing diagnosis 'Fatigue' for someone with anemia?

options.A: To ensure the patient stays on strict bed rest all day
options.B: To prove the patient is not sleeping well at night
options.C: To address reduced oxygen-carrying capacity in the blood
options.D: To document that the patient is refusing hospital food

explanation: Anemia means fewer red blood cells to ferry oxygen around. Less oxygen means less energy for the body—hence, deep fatigue! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h3)

question: Why is 'Risk for Infection' a top concern when a patient's white blood cell count is low?

options.A: The patient is forced to share a room with other sick individuals
options.B: The body lacks sufficient defense mechanisms to fight off invading pathogens
options.C: Intravenous lines always cause immediate blood infections
options.D: Hospital linens usually harbor resistant bacterial strains

explanation: White blood cells are our frontline soldiers against germs. When numbers are down, even friendly germs can become a big problem. Protection is key! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h3)

question: How should a nurse prioritize care goals for a patient with a serious blood disorder?

options.A: Prioritize patient food preferences over medication administration
options.B: Focus entirely on discharge teaching before checking vital signs
options.C: Treat minor skin rashes before managing low hemoglobin levels
options.D: Address immediate safety threats like severe bleeding or hypoxia first

explanation: ABC and safety always come first! Handling active bleeding or breathing trouble saves lives before we tackle other teaching. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h4)

question: What makes a patient care goal both effective and useful?

options.A: It includes specific, time-bound, and realistic criteria for success
options.B: It leaves room for guesswork regarding when care should stop
options.C: It uses complex medical jargon that only doctors can understand
options.D: It applies the exact same recovery timeline to every single patient

explanation: A good goal is clear and realistic so the whole healthcare team can easily tell if the patient is actually getting better. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h4)

question: A patient with very low platelets needs to shave. What should you hand them?
explanation: Safety first! An electric shaver prevents accidental nicks and cuts, keeping a low-platelet patient safe from bleeding. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h5)

question: Which nursing action is unsafe for a patient at high risk of bleeding?

options.A: Brushing teeth with a soft sponge
options.B: Using a sliding board for transfers

explanation: Rectal thermometers can easily scratch the delicate lining down there and trigger bleeding. Always choose a safer route! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h5)

question: During a blood transfusion, a patient suddenly gets back pain, chills, and fever. What is your very first action?

options.A: Call the hospital laboratory to double-check the patient's name
options.B: Stop the transfusion immediately and disconnect the tubing
options.C: Slow down the infusion rate and grab a warm cotton blanket
options.D: Administer a dose of oral paracetamol for the rising fever

explanation: Stop it right away! Cutting off the flow prevents any more incompatible blood from harming your patient during a reaction. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h6)

question: Why must you stay right by the patient during the first 15 minutes of a blood transfusion?

options.A: Hospital accreditation rules require physical presence to document vital signs
options.B: Most severe, life-threatening transfusion reactions occur during this initial window
options.C: Patients often feel lonely and anxious when receiving intravenous fluids
options.D: Pumps automatically lock out nurse access after fifteen minutes of running

explanation: Most bad reactions happen right at the beginning when the blood first hits circulation. Staying close lets you catch it instantly! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h6)

question: What is a key piece of advice for a patient going home with a chronic bleeding disorder?

options.A: Recognize and report early signs of bleeding like unusual bruising or blood in the stool
options.B: Avoid drinking water entirely to prevent fluid overload in the blood vessels
options.C: Stop taking all prescribed medications once you feel a slight energy improvement
options.D: Engage in high-contact sports to build up your physical strength and endurance

explanation: Teaching patients to spot early warning signs means they can get help before a minor bleed turns into a major emergency. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h7)

question: Which action best supports the emotional needs of a patient newly diagnosed with a blood disorder?

options.A: Leaving educational brochures on the bedside table and leaving
options.B: Providing active listening and validating their concerns
options.C: Directing all emotional questions strictly to the attending physician
options.D: Telling them not to worry because things could be worse

explanation: A new diagnosis is scary. Listening with empathy and validating their feelings builds trust and helps them cope better. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h7)

question: What should you do if your evaluation shows the patient's care goals were not met?

options.A: Assume the lab equipment is faulty and ignore the recorded results
options.B: Keep the exact same nursing interventions running without changes
options.C: Reassess the situation, identify the barriers, and modify the care plan
options.D: Discharge the patient anyway since the hospital stay has ended

explanation: Nursing is flexible! If a goal isn't met, we figure out what's blocking progress and tweak our care plan to try a new approach. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of the evaluation step in the nursing process?

options.A: To write a formal medical diagnosis for the physician to sign
options.B: To calculate the total financial cost of hospital supplies used
options.C: To decide which nurse will work the night shift over the weekend
options.D: To determine whether established patient care goals have been successfully met

explanation: Evaluation is just checking our report card: did our nursing care help the patient reach their health goals? [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h8)
